correctness.rationale: For the 36 vertex metric, independently enumerating cliques through size five gives (36,162,186,36,0); any larger clique would contain a five-clique. The tetrahedra are exactly the 36 neighborhood simplices and the 42 outside triangles are precisely the distinct alternating triples of the 21 listed hexagons. The two-spoke step equation leaves a=3,b=1, and the only spokeless hexagons are the three inner rings. In the neighborhood complex, each nonadjacent pair has a unique graph midpoint by girth, so neighbor-only triangles first collapse with their tetrahedra, then centered triangles collapse along their distance-two edges. Transport of the exceptional attaching maps along the resulting retraction is a homotopy-invariant CW attachment, not a collapse of the full Rips complex along edges now shared with exceptional triangles. Traversing either alternating triangle, the actual midpoint words trace its own hexagon. The second disk on each gives a sphere after the first disk, hence 21 spheres. With just the first disks, each outer-spoke hexagon has a free inner edge before adding the inner disks; collapse then leaves the outer circle and pendant spokes. Each transported inner loop traverses that circle once, with degree +1 (checked by the signed path substitution), so the first fills it and the two remaining give two more spheres. This proves the integral homotopy type independently of modular arithmetic. At radius one there are no graph triangles and the connected 36-vertex 54-edge graph has cycle rank 19.
residual_risks: Nonequivariant and fixed radius two on graph vertices; does not compute higher radii or persistence maps. The reviewed structural argument suffices without assuming that arbitrary group Tietze moves preserve a two-complex homotopy type.
